items.t: Paul Krugman Weighs In on AI Boom and Nvidia's Huang
items.d: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman, a City University of New York Graduate Center professor, argues that stock-market performance should not be confused with the health of the broader economy. items.t: The Economy Can't Be Held Hostage by Nvidia's Huang, Krugman Says
items.d: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman, a City University of New York Graduate Center professor, questions whether President Trump’s reported involvement in Jensen Huang’s reappointment as CEO reflected a “too big to fail” view of Nvidia. He argues that the economy should not depend on a single executive to keep a company stable. He speaks during an interview on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: Todd Blanche calls Nvidia a ‘good corporate citizen’ while dodging questions on investigation
items.d: Attorney General Todd Blanche praised Nvidia as a “good corporate citizen” while sidestepping questions about the Justice Department’s role in the president’s controversial decision to push for the reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang.
items.fullText: Trump administration Todd Blanche calls Nvidia a ‘good corporate citizen’ while dodging questions on investigation President Donald Trump had said the Justice Department had “exonerated” the chip giant’s newly reinstated CEO, Jensen Huang. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Blanche says he would have told Trump about any crimes Jensen Huang committed 01:22 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 1:37 PM EST By Dareh Gregorian and Helen Graham Attorney General Todd Blanche on Tuesday praised Nvidia as a “good corporate citizen” while sidestepping questions about the Justice Department’s role in the president’s controversial decision to push for the reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang. President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he’d spoken to Blanche and “they did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he himself was exonerated,” referring to Huang. Asked at an unrelated press conference about Trump’s remarks, Blanche said, “What the president said is that he talked to a lot of people going into the decision that he made to encourage the board to reinstate him,” before adding, “I’m not going to get into communications I have with the president about it.” He then said that what Trump was saying “is exactly right.” “To the extent that, that the department, that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said. NBC News previously reported that Trump sought Blanche and Vice President JD Vance’s help in convincing Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back. An administration official said the attorney general told the president that the DOJ had no evidence of wrongdoing by Huang or the company. items.t: Congress reacts with anger and skepticism about Jensen Huang reinstatement
items.d: Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle vowed to press ahead with investigations into the once-again Nvidia CEO, who’s scheduled to meet with them next week.
items.fullText: Congress Congress reacts with anger and skepticism about Jensen Huang reinstatement Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle vowed to press ahead with investigations into the once-again Nvidia CEO, who’s scheduled to meet with them next week. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Sen. Elizabeth Warren: Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO is ‘shocking’ 21:37 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 23, 2026, 1:37 PM EST / Updated Nov. 23, 2026, 6:19 PM EST By Dareh Gregorian and Brennan Leach The stock market was thrilled with the announcement that Jensen Huang was returning as CEO of Nvidia, but lawmakers on both sides of the aisle reacted with shock — and said they still expect him to answer questions next week on Capitol Hill . “You gotta be kidding me,” Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, told MS NOW when he learned of Huang’s reinstatement 11 days after he resigned in the wake of revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy. In its announcement, the board said it reached the decision after receiving “input from senior levels of the United States government” that his “reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Jensen Huang reinstated as NVIDIA CEO 02:27 “No national security risk? Based on what?” Cornyn asked in a post on X . President Donald Trump told CNBC he’d spoken to the board “directly and indirectly.” “One of the things the board wanted to know, is there a national security problem?” Trump said. “And after a lot of research, we — you know, we’ve been looking at this for more than a couple of days, right? This has been a story for a few weeks. We said no, it’s not a problem.” Lawmakers made clear they still need answers. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on May 14, 2026. Brendan Smialowski / AFP via Getty The Senate Banking Committee, chaired by Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., announced that Huang was scheduled to testify public

items.fullText: Merry Making: Play, Build and Create With NVIDIA Technologies This Holiday Season Get into the game, bring a creative project to life or try building a robot with NVIDIA platforms. November 23, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! The elves don’t have to be the only ones busy in the workshop this holiday season. With the lights twinkling and the gift wrap out, it’s the perfect time to give someone — or yourself — a spark to take a hobby to the next level. For some, that means diving into a new game. For others, it’s video editing or even building a robot. NVIDIA technologies offer something for everyone on Santa’s list. Read on to unwrap the details. Make Time for One More Game With the holiday break here, everyone can be online to score bragging rights or explore a world that’s only been seen in video game trailers. For some players, an upgrade means a desktop that brings out the detail in every scene. For others, it’s a laptop they can take along when visiting family, or a way to play in the cloud on a device they already own. The right setup depends on where and what to play: GeForce RTX 50 Series laptops and desktops power the action. Built on the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture, they feature fifth-generation Tensor Cores and fourth-generation RT Cores for AI-enhanced graphics, detailed ray-traced worlds and high frames-per-second gaming. NVIDIA RTX Spark PCs combine RTX graphics with NVIDIA’s full-stack AI platform on a single superchip, bringing decades of NVIDIA innovation to slim, premium laptops and compact desktops on the familiar Windows platform. One PC can handle every workflow, from accelerated creation and immersive gaming to powerful local AI — with a variety of designs and all-day battery life. See games in a new light with NVIDIA DLSS 5 technology, which boosts performance and enhances image quality. The newest feature, DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, infuses scenes with lifelike light

items.t: Major stock indexes soar on news of Huang’s return
items.d: Major U.S. stock indexes soared Monday to their best day since April 2025, as Wall Street cheered Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia.
items.fullText: Markets Stocks surge in best day since 2025, adding trillions in value after Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia Nvidia’s stock rose more than 30%, equivalent to about $950 billion of added value and the largest ever one-day gain in a company’s market capitalization. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Jensen Huang reinstated as NVIDIA CEO 02:27 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 23, 2026, 7:46 AM EST / Updated Nov. 23, 2026, 5:29 PM EST By Steve Kopack Major U.S. stock indexes soared Monday to their best day since April 2025, as Wall Street cheered Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia. The S&P 500 rallied 4.7%, while the Nasdaq 100 index surged almost 7%. The Dow, of which Nvidia is a large component, soared about 1,450 points. The broad moves higher also came as markets sought a rebound after AI-linked stocks dragged major indexes into correction territory Friday. The surprise announcement from Nvidia caused its stock to close up 31.5%, which added about $950 billion of value to the company, the largest one-day gain in market history. For perspective, the $950 billion in value Nvidia shares gained Monday is equivalent to more than twice the size of Coca-Cola, and just slightly less than the entire market capitalization of Walmart. It’s also the size of five Walt Disney’s, or three times the value of Bank of America. Nvidia’s surge also pushed the entire tech sector higher. Shares of companies in the sector collectively gained roughly $2.7 trillion in market value on Monday alone. Even with the day’s jump higher, Nvidia shares are still down 30% from their record high on Oct. 6. That drop leaves the company about $1.7 trillion smaller today than it was in early October. Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia came at the urging of President Donald Trump , who took credit for his return in an interview earlier on Monday morning.
